name: Ordering Width Takes Maxima on Products
statement: For nonempty $I\subseteq C$ and $J\subseteq D$, $\sigma(C\times D)=\max\{\sigma(C),\sigma(D)\}$ and $\sigma(C\times D;I\times J)=\max\{\sigma(C;I),\sigma(D;J)\}$.
proof: Conditioning a product to a concept of either factor gives the other factor, proving the lower bounds by minor monotonicity. For the upper bounds, use optimal factor orders and list the product by rows; minimal predecessor disagreements then occur purely in one factor.
